# MCP tools (`blazma-mcp`)

The MCP server exposes one tool per registry command plus a few session tools. Tool names are the command id with `.` replaced by `_` (`key.set` becomes `key_set`). Each result is the `CommandResult` as pretty JSON text (`ok`, `data`, `transactionId`, `warnings`, `error`); when `ok` is false the tool result has `isError = true`.

Effects: **readonly** runs immediately; **mutating** changes the project and can be undone; **destructive** needs the user's approval in the app (in headless mode it runs directly); **external** reads files outside the project and needs approval unless the path is in an allowed folder. Commands that write files (e.g. `animation_export`) only ever create new files, in the project folder or an allowed write folder (`--allow-write` / `BLAZMA_ALLOW_WRITE` headless); read folders never grant write.

## Session tools

| Tool | Where | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `project_info` | both | Name, file path and unsaved-changes flag of the open project. Call this first. Effect: readonly. |
| `project_save` | both | Save the project to its file (atomic, with read-back check), or to 'path' (save as). Effect: external (writes a file). |
| `task_begin` | both | Start a named task. All edits until task_finish are grouped, shown to the user as one unit and can be approved or rejected together. Effect: session. |
| `task_finish` | both | End the current task. In the app's Assisted mode the user then reviews it (Approve/Reject). Effect: session. |
| `task_status` | both | Your recent tasks with their state (running, review, approved, rejected) and the number of pending approvals. Effect: readonly. |
| `edit_undo` | both | Undo one of your own changes. Only the most recent change on the undo stack can be undone, by passing the transactionId its tool call returned. Effect: mutating. |
| `project_new` | headless only | Headless only: create a new .blazanim project containing the default mannequin character, save it and open it. Fails if the file exists. Effect: external (creates a file). |
| `project_open` | headless only | Headless only: open an existing .blazanim project (takes its session lock; fails if another process has it open). Effect: external (reads a file). |
| `project_close` | headless only | Headless only: close the open project and release its lock. Effect: session. |

No arguments.

### `animation_export`

Export a clip as a .glb animation (glTF 2.0 binary) plus a '<name>.blazma.json' sidecar (fps, loop, markers, events, root motion, bone map). The built-in mannequin gets a new file with a simple mesh; an imported character's original file is kept and the animation is appended. Writes files outside the project (the project itself is not changed); agents may only create new files. The written file is re-read and validated.

Effect: **readonly**. Command id: `animation.export`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string | yes | Clip id. (min length 1) |
| `characterId` | string | no | Character to export with (default: the first character using the clip's rig). (min length 1) |
| `path` | string | yes | Absolute path of the .glb to create; its folder must exist. (min length 1) |
| `rootMotion` | string | no | keep (default) \| in_place (remove the root's horizontal X/Z travel, keep height) \| in_place_all (remove all root translation). (min length 1) |
| `startFrame` | integer | no | First frame to export (default 0, or the loop start when the clip loops over part of its length); it becomes time 0 in the file. (min 0) |
| `endFrame` | integer | no | Last frame to export, inclusive (default: clip length, or the loop end when the clip loops over part of its length). (min 0) |
| `sidecar` | boolean | no | Also write '<name>.blazma.json' next to the .glb (default true). |
| `overwrite` | boolean | no | Replace existing files (default false). Ignored for agents, which can only create new files. |
| `validate` | boolean | no | Re-read the written file and validate it (default true). |

### `animation_validate`

Re-read an exported .glb and compare it with the clip frame by frame (position 1e-4 m, rotation 0.01°, scale 1e-4) and check its glTF structure, hierarchy and duration. Returns ok, max errors and issues.

Effect: **readonly**. Command id: `animation.validate`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Absolute path of the .glb. (min length 1) |
| `clipId` | string | yes | Clip id. (min length 1) |
| `characterId` | string | no | Character the file was exported with (default: as for animation.export). (min length 1) |

### `motion_generate`

Start generating a motion from a text prompt for a character. Runs in the background and returns a jobId; it does not change the project. Poll motion.job_status, then call motion.job_apply to add the result as a DRAFT clip (undoable), review it, and keep it with clip.accept_draft (or remove it with clip.delete). Provider: kimodo (local AI, must be installed by the user) by default; 'procedural' is a built-in keyword demo (walk, run, jump, wave, squat, idle), not AI. Body only: fingers and face are not generated.

Effect: **readonly**. Command id: `motion.generate`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `characterId` | string | yes | Character to animate (its rig must be humanoid-mapped). (min length 1) |
| `prompt` | string | yes | What the character should do, e.g. "a person walks forward". (min length 1) |
| `durationSeconds` | number | yes | Length in seconds (0.2–30). |
| `fps` | integer | no | Frame rate of the clip (default: the project frame rate). (min 1) |
| `seed` | integer | no | Random seed (default: a random one, returned and stored in the clip). (min 0) |
| `provider` | string | no | kimodo \| procedural. Default: kimodo, or the error provider_unavailable when it is not installed. (min length 1) |
| `name` | string | no | Clip name (default from the prompt). (min length 1) |
| `footCleanup` | boolean | no | Pin feet during ground contact (default true). |
| `reduceKeys` | boolean | no | Remove keys that linear interpolation reproduces within 0.1° / 0.5 mm (default true). |
| `loop` | boolean | no | Ask for a loopable motion (procedural only; Kimodo ignores constraints). |
| `inPlace` | boolean | no | Remove travel (procedural only). |

### `motion_job_apply`

Add a finished generation job's motion to the project as a new DRAFT clip (undoable). Returns clipId. Review it, edit keys, then clip.accept_draft.

Effect: **mutating**. Command id: `motion.job_apply`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jobId` | string | yes | Job id (state ready). (min length 1) |
| `name` | string | no | Clip name (default: the job's name). (min length 1) |

### `motion_job_cancel`

Cancel a running generation job (stops the Kimodo runner). Does not change the project.

Effect: **readonly**. Command id: `motion.job_cancel`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jobId` | string | yes | Job id. (min length 1) |

### `motion_job_status`

State of a generation job (running, ready, failed, cancelled, applied) with progress, warnings and, once applied, its clipId. Without jobId: all jobs. Headless only: waitSeconds blocks until the job finishes (max 600).

Effect: **readonly**. Command id: `motion.job_status`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `jobId` | string | no | Job id from motion.generate (omit to list all jobs). (min length 1) |
| `waitSeconds` | number | no | Wait up to this long for the job to finish (headless mode only; ignored in the app). |

### `motion_providers`

List the motion generation providers and diagnostics: is kimodo-runner configured and found, are the model files there, CPU/RAM/GPU (best effort, offline). Never downloads anything.

Effect: **readonly**. Command id: `motion.providers`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `probe` | boolean | no | Also start kimodo-runner briefly and ask it for its own diagnostics (only in headless mode; can take seconds). |

### `physics_analyze`

Balance analysis of a clip, frame by frame: centre of mass (COM), foot contacts, support polygon (convex hull of the touching sole points, XZ), signed margin of the tested point to the polygon (inside positive, metres) and balanced/unbalanced/airborne. Returns {summary:{unbalancedRanges…}, frames:[…]}. Does not change anything.

Effect: **readonly**. Command id: `physics.analyze`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string | yes | Clip id. (min length 1) |
| `characterId` | string | no | Character to evaluate the clip on (default: the first character using the clip's rig). (min length 1) |
| `startFrame` | integer | no | First frame (default 0). (min 0) |
| `endFrame` | integer | no | Last frame, inclusive (default: the clip's last frame). (min 0) |
| `summaryOnly` | boolean | no | Only the summary, no per-frame list. |
| `maxFrames` | integer | no | Most per-frame entries to return (default 120, max 2000); the rest is summarized. (min 1) |
| `metric` | string | no | com (static, default) \| zmp (zero-moment point, uses COM acceleration) \| capture (capture point, uses COM velocity). (min length 1) |
| `minMargin` | number | no | Margin (m) a frame needs to count as balanced (default 0). |
| `contactHeight` | number | no | Sole points at most this high above the ground (m) can touch (default 0.03). |

### `physics_auto_balance`

Move the COM inside the support polygon (by 'margin') on unbalanced frames by shifting the hips horizontally; supporting feet stay planted (legs re-solved with IK). Keys the pelvis translation (and leg rotations of unpinned supporting legs) on corrected frames; every other frame keeps exactly its original pose (frames between the surrounding original keys are keyed with their original values). Refuses (no_leg_ik / track_locked / track_muted) when a supporting foot could not stay planted, unless allowFootSlide. At most 5000 frames and 200,000 keys (too_large). One undo step. Returns before/after margins per frame.

Effect: **mutating**. Command id: `physics.auto_balance`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string | yes | Clip id. (min length 1) |
| `characterId` | string | no | Character to evaluate the clip on (default: the first character using the clip's rig). (min length 1) |
| `frames` | string | no | Comma-separated frames to correct; omit to use startFrame/endFrame. (min length 1) |
| `startFrame` | integer | no | First frame (default 0). (min 0) |
| `endFrame` | integer | no | Last frame, inclusive (default: the clip's last frame). (min 0) |
| `margin` | number | no | Distance (m) to keep the COM inside the polygon (default 0.02, max 0.5). |
| `maxShift` | number | no | Largest hip shift (m, default 0.3, max 1). |
| `allowFootSlide` | boolean | no | Correct anyway when a supporting foot has no leg IK chain or its leg tracks are locked/muted (that foot may slide). |

### `physics_com`

Centre of mass and static balance of a character: its working pose, or a clip frame when 'clipId' is given (with velocity, ZMP and capture point). Returns {com, totalMass, massSource, contacts, polygon, margin, state}. Does not change anything.

Effect: **readonly**. Command id: `physics.com`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `characterId` | string | yes | Character id. (min length 1) |
| `clipId` | string | no | Evaluate this clip instead of the working pose. (min length 1) |
| `frame` | integer | no | Clip frame (default 0). (min 0) |
| `segments` | boolean | no | Also list each segment's mass and centre. |

### `physics_secondary_motion`

Bake follow-through / overlap: the chosen bones lag behind the clip's motion like damped springs (stiffness k 1/s², damping c 1/s; mass-independent, stable at any fps). Writes rotation keys on every frame of the range; frames outside it keep exactly their original pose (one undo step). Locked or muted bones are left out (their children follow them as played back). Give 'bones' and/or 'preset'. Work is capped: frames × bones × sub-steps (≤ 1/240 s each) ≤ 2,000,000 and ≤ 200,000 keys (too_large).

Effect: **mutating**. Command id: `physics.secondary_motion`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string | yes | Clip id. (min length 1) |
| `characterId` | string | no | Character to evaluate the clip on (default: the first character using the clip's rig). (min length 1) |
| `bones` | string | no | Comma-separated bone names or ids, parent before child for a chain. (min length 1) |
| `preset` | string | no | spine \| head \| arms (humanoid-mapped bones). (min length 1) |
| `stiffness` | number | no | Spring stiffness k (1/s², default 150 ≈ 1.9 Hz; max 10000). |
| `damping` | number | no | Damping c (1/s, default 12; damping ratio = c / (2√k)). |
| `maxAngle` | number | no | Largest lag in degrees (default 30). |
| `startFrame` | integer | no | First frame (default 0). (min 0) |
| `endFrame` | integer | no | Last frame, inclusive (default: the clip's last frame). (min 0) |

### `physics_trajectories`

Per-frame model-space paths of a clip for drawing: centre of mass, hips (pelvis) and/or feet (ankles). Returns arrays of [x,y,z]. Does not change anything.

Effect: **readonly**. Command id: `physics.trajectories`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clipId` | string | yes | Clip id. (min length 1) |
| `characterId` | string | no | Character to evaluate the clip on (default: the first character using the clip's rig). (min length 1) |
| `what` | string | no | com \| feet \| hips \| all (default all). (min length 1) |
| `startFrame` | integer | no | First frame (default 0). (min 0) |
| `endFrame` | integer | no | Last frame, inclusive (default: the clip's last frame). (min 0) |
